Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business

contribution noun

money given as one’s share

also contributions, one’s share, share of the cost, chip in, whip-round, collection

classical

Liv. 5.25.5: dē conlātiōne … stipis vērius quam decumae
Tac. Germ. 29 (Lewis & Short)

collātiō, collātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a contribution, a collection of money

Money brought together for a common purpose, from cōnferre, to contribute (see donate): to chip in is pecūniam cōnferre. Its other senses are a bringing together and, in Cicero, a comparison or an analogy (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • symbola, symbolae f. — one’s share of the bill for a shared meal

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Ter. And. 88; Ter. Eun. 540: ut dē symbolīs essēmus, to dine on shares

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; posteā Gell.)

    From Greek; symbolam dare, to pay one’s share. A dinner where everyone pays a share is had dē symbolīs.

  • 1collēcta: long e (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). From colligō, participle collēctus, long by Lachmann’s law, as lēctus. Ruling: Lachmann’s law: āctus, lēctus, frāctus.

    collēcta1, collēctae f. — a contribution (to a shared meal)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.233: collēctam ā convīvā exigere (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero’s word for what Terence calls a symbola (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • “eho quid Pamphilus?” “quid? symbolam dedit, cēnāvit.”

    “Well, what about Pamphilus?” “What about him? He paid his share and had dinner.”Ter. And. 88–89

See also donate, fund, pay, divide.

SourcesLewis & Short: collatio · Lewis & Short: symbola · Lewis & Short: collecta · Lewis & Short: confero

Terence and Livy checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (11 November 2026); the quotation from Livy keeps that edition’s spelling conlātiōne.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
